findings.summary: The tests do not cover the legacy-page cases the brief names. All three tests (new page, update in place, status patch) start from a page that the new code wrote itself. No test updates in place, or status-patches, a page that carries the legacy `memorycard_*` keys. A legacy page patched for status keeps its legacy keys, and no test pins or states that outcome.
evidence: page_keys_test.go promotes first with the new code in all three tests, so the starting pages only ever carry `source_*` keys.
propagate_cards.go:127-131 patches only `status` and `related` through `patchedFrontmatter`, so a legacy page keeps `memorycard_*` after a status patch.
UpdateInPlace (update.go:139-162) rewrites the whole page, so an update in place does replace the keys on a legacy page that the sidecar already tracks. No test pins this.

UpdateInPlace refuses legacy pages the sidecar does not track, because `isOwnUnrecordedWrite` compares the full render. The ownership checks themselves (`isOwnUnrecordedWrite`, `isOwnUnrecordedUpdate`, `corroboratingFrontmatter`) were not changed or verified for memorycard pages.
S6 (c), the migration of legacy pages, is a separate task, so this is a coverage gap in this commit, not a proven defect.

findings.summary: `emitEngramPage` still writes `engram_*` keys including `engram_sync_id`, and the `EngramSyncID` field is still rendered. S6 (b) says `engram_sync_id` is not written and every page carries `source: memorycard`. If any Engram-source write path is still reachable, it contradicts the spec. S6 (b) itself notes this holds only after S10 makes memorycard the only writer.
evidence: page_style.go:133 sets `EngramSyncID: m.SyncID`, and frontmatter.go:200 renders it.
The new test only exercises memorycard promotion via `--source memorycard`.
The `engramSyncIDField` entry in `update.go:448` is still needed by `corroboratingFrontmatter` while Engram pages exist.

findings.summary: `source_type` is written unquoted and raw from `m.Type`, so an empty type renders as `source_type: ` and an unusual type string is not YAML-escaped. The old frontmatter writer did the same, so this is not new, and memorycard types are a closed set.
evidence: `quoteYAML` is applied to the title but not to `source_type`.
I could not run bash, so I could not read `git show c303b6f7`. I judged the code at the worktree target directly. The tests were not run.

Read page_style.go: `emitCardPage` renders `source`, `source_id`, `source_type`, `source_revision` and `project`, with no `memorycard_*` and no `engram_*` keys, and `cardStatus` is shared with the status patch.

Read page_identity.go: `fieldOf`, `identityOf` and `revisionOf` read the store-agnostic keys first and fall back to the legacy keys per field, so pages written with the new keys are still found by the scans.

Read update.go: `UpdateInPlace` rewrites the whole page. `frontmatterRevision` and `pageRevision` go through `revisionOf`, so they read `source_revision`. `corroboratingFrontmatter` blanks `source_revision` and `source_type`.
Read propagate_cards.go: the status patch rewrites only `status` and `related`.

Read page_keys_test.go: it asserts the four store-agnostic keys, the absence of every legacy key including `engram_sync_id`, and a single `source:` line, for a new page, an update in place (revision 4) and a status patch.
